direction.premise: Two tiny, stubborn wizards have no idea how badly their own spell combinations will misbehave, but the duel still reads at a glance.
direction.composition: A pixel-art stone arena fills the phone. The player's movement thumb rests at the lower left and three spell buttons at the lower right; the top carries two slim health readings.
direction.shapeLanguage: Wizard silhouettes are large hats on tiny coats; masonry is made of offset broken rectangles and the runes live in compact paper pieces rather than generic glossy cards.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: The courtyard remains hand-composed pixel stone; the mage is now a manually layered pixel costume with safe account-drawing cameo patches and MASKOT-dependent ears, helmets, hat and coat geometry.
direction.paletteLogic: The arena uses muddy mineral greens and warm brown shadows to keep peach projectiles, gold sparks and a second reddish wizard distinguishable without electric neon.
direction.typography: Headings use an old-book serif as a restrained signboard; interface text uses sturdy system sans, short Russian instructions and plain names such as Шар больнее.
direction.signature: A genuinely individual little pixel wizard carries the PocketWorks account's actual drawing or animal MASKOT, while a few spells add visible gear without replacing their identifying ears and coat.
direction.distinction: Unlike VENETS parchment political screens and MEAT.EXE first-person corridors, Perekos has an unframed bird's-eye arcade arena with bottom-corner direct spell buttons.

architecture.primaryVerb: Keep one thumb on the movement circle and hold the other on the fire spell while avoiding incoming bolts.
architecture.physicalFeedback: Projectiles appear instantly and strike with small bright pixel bursts; shield casts emit an expanding ring and the wizard dashes between positions.
architecture.spatialRationale: The uninterrupted portrait battle canvas occupies the center, while health readings above and two thumb clusters below preserve visibility of attacks and cover.

comparisons.spatialDifference: The first-person apartment owns the entire frame with a gun overlay, while Perekos uses an overhead stone battleground and explicit two-sided health labels.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Perekos demands two-thumb movement and casting with between-round rune selection instead of room exploration, discovery and first-person gun interaction.

comparisons.spatialDifference: MEAT.EXE is a full-screen first-person flesh labyrinth, whereas this title places tiny top-down characters and handmade masonry under a visible light-colored rune sheet.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Holding projectile fire and selecting permanent between-round upgrades replaces first-person weapon aiming, pickups and navigating a procedural maze.

comparisons.spatialDifference: The 5x5 tactical game uses a distinct framed board and its order planning layer; Perekos keeps an unframed real-time moving world behind contextual result sheets.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Real-time dodging, spell cooldowns and hold-to-fire differ from ordered tactical commands and simultaneous phase resolution.

production.renderer: Quick PWA uses a standalone 400x620 Canvas 2D low-resolution scene with deterministic pre-rendered masonry; simple DOM controls remain crisp and accessible.
production.focalAsset: The hero object is an avatar-derived mage sprite authored with Canvas pixel rectangles: its species, hat, clothing, drawing cameo and signed-in portrait all come from validated account data, while rune effects add a removable final layer.

motion.character: Movement and spells are instant and snappy, while robe and hat gently bob to keep the character alive and distinguish standing still from a frozen sprite.
motion.action: A player touches the fire button while moving and aiming away from the opponent to direct a sequence of small magic bolts.
motion.anticipation: The spell action has intentionally almost no wind-up for responsiveness; the hand-held staff is already posed toward the enemy.
motion.response: The spell appears in the same simulated tick, and a small gold muzzle bloom plus a short synthesized sound makes firing unambiguous.
motion.followThrough: The bolt leaves a short luminous trail and a tiny pixel burst on masonry or the enemy; the shield ring expands briefly before settling.
motion.interruption: Dash, shield and attack inputs are sampled in a fixed update loop; release or new direction cancels ongoing continuous casting without queued commands.
motion.reducedMotion: Reduced-motion mode retains hit blocks, ring outlines, projectile positions and score/health changes without CSS transitions and excess movement.

evidence.expectedChange: Starting the duel reveals a personalized hero instead of a generic sprite, and a valid PocketWorks MASKOT is recognizable in the hero canvas, HUD portrait and the live battle.
